original: मनवश्चाभवन्नत्र स्वायम्भुवमुखा मुने । चतुर्दशैते कथिता लोकानां परिपालकाः ॥

translation: The fourteen Manus, headed by Svayambhuva, were established by cosmic order as the protectors and guides of humanity.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.1): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

original: एक आसीद्यजुर्वेदस्तं चतुर्धा व्यकल्पयत् । व्यासः पराशरोदारः शिष्यान् स समपादयत् ॥
transliteration: eka āsīdyajurvedastaṃ caturdhā vyakalpayat | vyāsaḥ parāśarodāraḥ śiṣyān sa samapādayat ||
translation: Originally there was one Veda; the noble Vyasa partitioned it fourfold—Rig, Yajur, Sama, and Atharva—and taught them to his disciples.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.2): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

original: पैलाय संहितां प्रादादृग्वेदाख्यां महायशाः । वैशम्पायननाम्ने तु यजुर्वेदं समर्पयत् ॥
transliteration: pailāya saṃhitāṃ prādādṛgvedākhyāṃ mahāyaśāḥ | vaiśampāyananāmne tu yajurvedaṃ samarpayat ||
translation: To Paila he gave the Rigveda Samhita; to Vaisampayana he entrusted the Yajurveda.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.3): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

original: जैमिनये सामवेदं सुमन्तवेऽथर्वणम् । इतिहासपुराणानि सूताय प्रददौ प्रभुः ॥
transliteration: jaiminaye sāmavedaṃ sumantave'tharvaṇam | itihāsapurāṇāni sūtāya pradadau prabhuḥ ||
translation: To Jaimini he gave the Samaveda, to Sumantu the Atharvaveda, and the Epics and Puranas he entrusted to Romaharshana the Suta.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.4): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

original: यथा नदीनदाः सर्वे समुद्रे यान्ति संस्थितिम् । तथैवाश्रमिणः सर्वे गृहस्थे यान्ति संस्थितिम् ॥
transliteration: yathā nadīnadāḥ sarve samudre yānti saṃsthitim | tathaivāśramiṇaḥ sarve gṛhasthe yānti saṃsthitim ||
translation: Even as all rivers and streams find their resting place in the ocean, so all other stages of life rely upon the householder for sustenance.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.5): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

original: अतिथियस्य भग्नाशो गृहात्प्रतिनिवर्तते । स तस्मै दुष्कृतं दत्त्वा पुण्यमादाय गच्छति ॥
transliteration: atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivartate | sa tasmai duṣkṛtaṃ dattvā puṇyamādāya gacchati ||
translation: He from whose home a guest turns away disappointed transfers his demerits to the host and carries away all the host's virtues.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.6): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

layers.content: Wilson provides classical critical analysis of this verse from Vishnu Purana Book 3, highlighting its alignment with traditional Vedantic principles.

transliteration: śrāddhaṃ kurvanti ye bhaktyā pitṛṇāṃ tṛptihetave | teṣāṃ tuṣṭāḥ prayacchati pitaro vāñchitaṃ phalam ||
translation: Those who perform ancestral rites (Shraddha) with devotion gladden their ancestors, who bestow longevity, wisdom, and peace.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.7): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

layers.content: Wilson provides classical critical analysis of this verse from Vishnu Purana Book 3, highlighting its alignment with traditional Vedantic principles.

original: सदाचारेण युक्तानां ब्राह्मणानां प्रशस्यते । तपसां च फलं विष्णोः प्रसादेन प्रवर्तते ॥
transliteration: sadācāreṇa yuktānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ praśasyate | tapasāṃ ca phalaṃ viṣṇoḥ prasādena pravartate ||
translation: Ethical conduct is the crown of spiritual life; the fruit of all austerity blossoms only through the grace of Lord Vishnu.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.8): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

original: नास्तिकानां च संवादो धर्मविप्लवकारकः । सत्यं ज्ञानं परं ब्रह्म विष्णुरेवेति संस्मरेत् ॥
transliteration: nāstikānāṃ ca saṃvādaḥ dharmaviplavakārakaḥ | satyaṃ jñānaṃ paraṃ brahma viṣṇureveti saṃsmaret ||
translation: Disputation born of nihilism disrupts dharma; one should continually remember that Truth, Wisdom, and Supreme Brahman are Vishnu alone.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.9): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.

layers.content: Wilson provides classical critical analysis of this verse from Vishnu Purana Book 3, highlighting its alignment with traditional Vedantic principles.

original: तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन धर्मं सेवेत मानवः । धर्म एव सहायोऽस्ति परलोके तरिष्यतः ॥
transliteration: tasmātsarvaprayatnena dharmaṃ seveta mānavaḥ | dharma eva sahāyo'sti paraloke tariṣyataḥ ||
translation: Therefore, with all one's might, one should practice Dharma; for Dharma alone is the friend that accompanies the soul into the beyond.
meaning: Tritiya Amsa — Manvantaras, Vedas & Origin of Dharma (Verse 3.10): Authentic classical exposition of Vaishnava philosophy.
